title: Arbitrary base change for smooth ambient duality
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and let $N\geq1$ satisfy $NA=0$, with $N$ invertible on the schemes in question, as in [thm-asd-smooth-tensor]. All categories are the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ of [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], not completed or constructible categories. For a morphism $v$, write $v^*$ for exact etale inverse image on constant-coefficient module sheaves, extended degreewise to complexes. Let $f:X\to S$ be smooth, separated, compactifiable and of pure relative dimension $d$, between Noetherian schemes, as in [thm-asd-smooth-tensor]. Let $g:S'\to S$ be any morphism of Noetherian schemes, and put $X'=X\times_S S'$, with projections $g':X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to S'$. Use $Rf_!$ of [def-amb-etale-compact-support] and its right adjoint $f^\times$ of [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], and similarly for $f'$. The canonical morphism $\beta_{f,g,K}:g'^*f^\times K\to f'^\times g^*K$, obtained by transposing the pullback of the counit through compact-support base change, is an isomorphism for every $K\in D(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. At $K=A_S$ it gives $b:g'^*\omega_f\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{f'}$, where $\omega_f=f^\times A_S$. If $\phi_{f,K}:f^*K\otimes_A^L\omega_f\to f^\times K$ denotes the canonical tensor map of [thm-asd-smooth-tensor], then
$$\beta_{f,g,K}\circ g'^*\phi_{f,K}=\phi_{f',g^*K}\circ(1\otimes b)$$
after identifying $g'^*(f^*K\otimes_A^L\omega_f)$ with $f'^*g^*K\otimes_A^Lg'^*\omega_f$. The derived tensor is the ringed-site tensor construction of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] applied to the constant ring on the etale site.

proof.text: First supply the missing unbounded refinement argument, rather than invoke the bounded-below compactification-comparison lemma, whose source explicitly proves only the bounded-below case. Work throughout with the fixed finite torsion ring $A$ and the unbounded candidates of [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. First derive ordinary direct-image composition without an invertible-prime assumption. The derived adjunctions of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] give, for composable $a,b$, natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(L,Rb_*Ra_*K)=\operatorname{Hom}(b^*L,Ra_*K)=\operatorname{Hom}(a^*b^*L,K)=\operatorname{Hom}((ba)^*L,K)=\operatorname{Hom}(L,R(ba)_*K)$, using the canonical inverse-image composition comparison. Yoneda gives the counit-preserving isomorphism $Rb_*Ra_*\cong R(ba)_*$. For three maps both hom-bijection composites apply the three adjunctions in the same order; associativity of inverse-image composition makes them equal. Identity maps give the identity bijection. These composition comparisons require no invertibility condition and are the ones used in this proof. For a proper refinement $u:T_1\to T_2$ with $uj_1=j_2$, let $V=T_1\times_{T_2}X$, $b:V\hookrightarrow T_1$, $p:V\to X$, and $s:X\hookrightarrow V$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-section], $s$ identifies $X$ with an open-and-closed subscheme of $V$ and $ps=1$. Thus $s_!=s_*$ on sheaves (both are the original sheaf on that component and zero on its complement) and this functor is exact. Extension by zero for nested opens composes degreewise: inside $X$ both stalks are the stalk of $K$, and elsewhere both are zero. Open base change from [lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-modules] consequently gives $b^*j_{1!}K=s_!K$. Proper base change [lem-kun-proper-base-change-torsion-ring] and the direct-image composition just derived, give the canonical isomorphism $j_2^*Ru_*j_{1!}K\cong Rp_*s_!K\cong K$ for every unbounded $K$. Define $\alpha_{u,K}:j_{2!}K\to Ru_*j_{1!}K$ by the open adjunction of [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality], transposing the inverse of this isomorphism. Over $X$ it is the identity under the displayed comparison. At a geometric point of $T_2\setminus X$, proper base change identifies the target with derived direct image on the fibre of the pullback of $j_{1!}K$. That pullback is zero: the fibre does not meet $j_1(X)$, so each of its stalk complexes is zero by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks] and exact inverse image. The source stalk is also zero. Exact geometric stalks [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk], geometric conservativity [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative], and [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] now prove that $\alpha_u$ is invertible on all of $D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. This tests isomorphisms degree by degree, not equality of derived morphisms by stalks. For refinements $u,v$, transpose both $\alpha_{vu}$ and $(Rv_*\alpha_u)\alpha_v$ under $j_{3!}\dashv j_3^*$: proper-exchange pasting [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] identifies both restrictions with the inverse of $j_3^*R(vu)_*j_{1!}K\cong K$. The adjunction bijection proves their equality; the identity case is the same calculation. For base change, write $g_i:T_i'\to T_i$, $h:X'\to X$, and $z_i:g_i^*j_{i!}\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_{i!}h^*$ for the open comparisons, with primes on all pulled-back morphisms understood. The required equation is $Ru'_*z_1\circ\operatorname{Ex}_u\circ g_2^*\alpha_u=\alpha_{u'}\circ z_2$. Precompose with $z_2^{-1}$ and transpose under $j'_{2!}\dashv j_2'{}^*$. The restriction of the left side is the inverse open restriction of proper exchange for $u'$: the extra exchange for $u$ cancels its inverse in the definition of $\alpha_u$, by proper-exchange pasting. This is the restriction defining the right side. The mate-pasting statement and the adjunction bijection prove the equation. Finally [prop-nagata-compactification-category] supplies common refinements and equalizers over an arbitrary Noetherian base (not just over a field), and preserves refinements under arbitrary base change. Apply $Rr_{2*}$ to $\alpha_u$ and the same direct-image composition to compare $Rr_{1*}j_{1!}$ with $Rr_{2*}j_{2!}$. The identity and composition equations just proved, followed by a common equalizing refinement, make comparisons independent of choices and give the cocycle law. These are the unbounded, base-change-compatible comparisons used below.

source.place: Proof paragraphs 1–2: repair of the explicitly bounded-below argument using unbounded proper exchange (Stacks 0F0C)

proof.text: Next prove unbounded composition on the same candidates. In a Cartesian square with proper $p:\overline X\to\overline Y$ and open $v:Y\hookrightarrow\overline Y$, write $V=\overline X\times_{\overline Y}Y$, $b:V\hookrightarrow\overline X$ and $p_Y:V\to Y$. The restriction $p_Y$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b). For any unbounded $N$ on $V$, define $\lambda_{p,v,N}:v_!Rp_{Y*}N\to Rp_*b_!N$ by $v_!\dashv v^*$, transposing the inverse of proper exchange $v^*Rp_*b_!N\cong Rp_{Y*}b^*b_!N=Rp_{Y*}N$. Over $Y$ this is the identity; outside $Y$, proper base change [lem-kun-proper-base-change-torsion-ring] makes the target zero, since the fibre misses $V$ and the pulled-back extension is zero by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks]. The exactness and cohomology detection nodes of Step 1 show $\lambda$ is invertible for arbitrary $N$, without any truncation. For $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{h}S$, choose a compactification $Y\xrightarrow{v}\overline Y\xrightarrow{\bar h}S$, and compactify $vf$ as $X\xrightarrow{a}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}\overline Y$, using [thm-nagata-compactification]. The factorization $X\hookrightarrow V\xrightarrow{p_Y}Y$ is a compactification of $f$. Substitute $N=(X\hookrightarrow V)_!M$ into $\lambda$ and apply $R\bar h_*$; nested open extensions compose degreewise and the adjunction-based direct-image composition in Step 1 identifies the proper factors. This constructs $Rh_!Rf_!\cong R(hf)_!$. The interchanger $\lambda$ is the mate, under the open adjunctions, of the inverse proper-exchange isomorphism just displayed. Therefore its equations for consecutive proper maps, consecutive open maps, and change of base are respectively the two pasting equations and the change-of-adjunction equation of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]; proper-exchange pasting itself follows by applying that statement to the inverse-image composition comparison of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange]. This verifies coherence of the actual maps: after transposition, each equation is the equality of the pasted inverse-image comparison with the comparison for the outer rectangle, rather than an inference from invertibility or stalkwise equality. Explicitly, for consecutive proper maps $P\xrightarrow{p}Q\xrightarrow{q}R$ and an open $v:W\hookrightarrow R$, write $b_Q:Q_W\hookrightarrow Q$ and $b_P:P_W\hookrightarrow P$ for the pulled-back opens, and $p_W,q_W$ for the proper restrictions. Under direct-image composition the interchanger identity is $\lambda_{qp,v,N}=Rq_*\lambda_{p,b_Q,N}\circ\lambda_{q,v,Rp_{W*}N}$. For consecutive opens $U\xrightarrow{w}W\xrightarrow{v}R$ and a proper $p:P\to R$, let $p_W:P_W\to W$ and $c:P_U\hookrightarrow P_W$. The other identity is $\lambda_{p,vw,N}=\lambda_{p,v,c_!N}\circ v_!\lambda_{p_W,w,N}$. Transposing these displayed composites under $(vw)_!\dashv(vw)^*$ or $v_!\dashv v^*$ gives, in each case, the inverse of the proper exchange for the outer rectangle; clauses (1) and (2) of the mate-pasting lemma give precisely these inverses. For compatibility with $\alpha_u$, first insert the base-change equation displayed in Step 1 and then transpose under the remaining open adjunction: both paths are the inverse proper exchange on the restricted complex $N$. Clause (3) gives equality before transposition. This also verifies compatibility with a further change of base, using the same displayed refinement equation and the pasted proper-exchange equality. For three morphisms expand all candidates into proper and open factors. The two orders of moving open factors past proper factors use exactly those interchanger equations; the remaining proper reassociations agree by the hom-bijection associativity checked in Step 1, and the open reassociations are degreewise identities. Hence both parenthesizations give the same composition map. Changing compactifications gives the same map by the refinement equation and common refinements of Step 1. This proves the composition and base-change coherence on the unbounded category needed in Steps 3, 6 and 7, without citing the bounded-below compactification-comparison assertion.

source.place: Composition paragraph: explicit unbounded replacement and interchanger mate calculation; Stacks 0F0C and mate-pasting clauses 1–3

proof.text: Choose a compactification $f=rj$. Its pullback $f'=r'j'$ is again a compactification. Put $C_{f,g}:g^*Rf_!\to Rf'_!g'^*$ equal to proper exchange for $r$, followed by $Rr'_*$ of the inverse of the extension-by-zero comparison. Proper exchange is invertible on every unbounded $A$-complex by [lem-kun-proper-base-change-torsion-ring]; extension-by-zero base change is invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-modules]. The latter descends degreewise because inverse image and open extension by zero are exact. Thus $C$ is invertible on the entire category, without a bounded-below reduction. The unbounded refinement comparisons proved in Step 1 identify the compact-support candidates. Define $\beta_{f,g,K}$ to be the adjunct under $Rf'_!\dashv f'^\times$ of $g^*\epsilon_{f,K}\circ C_{f,g,f^\times K}^{-1}$. In symbols, its defining equation is $\epsilon_{f',g^*K}\,Rf'_!(\beta_{f,g,K})=g^*\epsilon_{f,K}\,C_{f,g,f^\times K}^{-1}$. The comparisons used below obey pasting on these same unbounded categories: proper exchange is the mate of inverse-image composition, so its pasting follows from [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]; the etale extension comparison is the conjugate specified in [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map], so its pasting follows from that same lemma. For a composite $hv$, expanding $Rf_!$ into proper direct image and open extension, the two pasted factors are therefore the proper exchange for the composite square and the open comparison for the composite square. Reassociate the proper factors and use the refinement comparisons of Step 1 and the composition construction of Step 2; this gives $C_{hv,g}=C_{h,g}Rv_!$ followed by $Rh'_!C_{v,g_h}$, with the pullback composition identifications inserted. Horizontal pasting gives $C_{f,gh}=C_{f',h}\circ h^*C_{f,g}$, again with the inverse-image composition inserted. These are equalities of the canonical comparisons, not deductions from their invertibility.

source.place: Proof paragraph 1; Stacks Tags 0F0C and 03S6 replace the mis-cited projection formula

proof.text: Apply the current statement of [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection] with its coefficient ring equal to the given finite commutative ring $A$, $V=\overline X$, $T=S$, $L=j_!M$ and $K=N$. The compactification has $r$ proper of finite type; its source is Noetherian because it is finite type over the Noetherian base $S$. Both $M$ and $N$ are arbitrary unbounded ordinary small-etale complexes, exactly as required by that statement. Its specified ordered projection map is $Rr_*(\sigma)\circ\mathrm{PF}_r(j_!M,N)\circ\sigma$, from $N\otimes^LRr_*j_!M$ to $Rr_*(r^*N\otimes^Lj_!M)$; all three factors are isomorphisms. Use the open comparison $j_!(j^*r^*N\otimes^LM)\cong r^*N\otimes^Lj_!M$ to obtain the canonical compact-support map $N\otimes^LRf_!M\to Rf_!(f^*N\otimes^LM)$. Thus its inverse has precisely the order used by the tensor-map counit in Steps 5 and 9. The open comparison can equivalently be written $j_!(M\otimes^Lj^*N)\cong j_!M\otimes^LN$, with $N$ here a complex on the ambient scheme; the two orders are related by the signed tensor symmetries specified in the cited proper projection statement. The underived comparison $j_!(M\otimes j^*N)\to j_!M\otimes N$ is defined by the open adjunction [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality]: its restriction is the identity on $M\otimes j^*N$. Applying it termwise gives the tensor-complex comparison. For its derived form use flat K-flat representatives [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]; by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks], at a geometric stalk inside the open it is identity on the total tensor complex, and outside it both sides are zero. The stalk tensor isomorphism [lem-pod-etale-stalk-tensor-scalar] and exactness of geometric stalks [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk] show that these degreewise identifications give the derived comparison; [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal] supplies its restriction inside the open. For precision, check the open base-change square before passing to the derived category: choose flat K-flat representatives, whose inverse images remain flat K-flat by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Open extension preserves flatness and K-flatness: its stalks are the original flat modules or zero, and tensoring its extended complex with an acyclic complex is the extension of the tensor with the restricted acyclic complex, which is acyclic by exactness of restriction and extension. In each degree both composites in the square send a tensor of germs inside the open to that same tensor of pulled-back germs; outside the open both are zero. Faithfulness of geometric stalks on maps of sheaves gives equality of these chain maps degree by degree (the image of their difference has zero stalks, so conservativity applied to its map to zero makes that image zero). Consequently the square commutes after localization at quasi-isomorphisms. No faithfulness of stalk functors on derived morphisms is asserted. For $r$, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence], applied to constant $A$-ringed etale topoi, gives the projection/base-change square for $\mathrm{PF}_r(j_!M,N)$ in the order $(j_!M,N)$. Conjugating this square by the two canonical tensor symmetries gives the square for the ordered map of [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection]. Indeed on K-flat tensor complexes each symmetry sends a homogeneous tensor of degrees $(p,q)$ to $(-1)^{pq}$ times the swapped tensor. Exact pullback preserves those degrees and that scalar, so its tensor comparison commutes with the signed swaps as a chain-map equality. Naturality of symmetry with respect to the exchange map gives the other side of the conjugated square. Pasting this square with the open one proves that the compact-support projection formula commutes with $C_{f,g}$, on arbitrary complexes.

source.place: Proof final sentence: projection formula/counit rectangle; Stacks 0E48 and 07A4

proof.text: For $q:\mathbf P^1_S\to S$, apply [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction] with the given finite commutative ring $A$ and integer $N$: $NA=0$ and $N$ is invertible on $S$. This input explicitly states an adjunction on the ordinary unbounded small-etale categories, using $L_P(1)=\mu_{N,P}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/N}A$ and its Kummer-normalized trace $t_q=\operatorname{pr}_2b_q^{-1}$. No pro-etale inverse-limit coefficient object is substituted. Choose the compactification $(1,q)$; thus $Rq_!=Rq_*$. Compare its supplied right adjoint $G_q=q^*(-)\otimes^LL_P(1)[2]$ with $q^\times$ by the unique adjunction-preserving isomorphism, so the counit is exactly $\epsilon_{q,K}=(1_K\otimes t_q)\mathrm{PF}^{-1}$. Use the same counit-preserving comparison on the pulled-back projective line. The finite-twist pullback of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] supplies $\rho:g_P^*L_P(1)\cong L_{P'}(1)$. Let $B=Rq'_*(\rho[2])\operatorname{Ex}_{q,L_P(1)[2]}$. The ordinary finite P1 input states compatibility of its decomposition and trace with this canonical exchange. More explicitly that decomposition compatibility reads $B\,g^*b_q=b_{q'}(\rho_S[2]\oplus1)$, where $\rho_S:g^*L_S(1)\cong L_{S'}(1)$. Multiply by the inverse decomposition and project to the second summand: $t_{q'}B=\operatorname{pr}_2(\rho_S[2]\oplus1)(g^*b_q)^{-1}=g^*(\operatorname{pr}_2b_q^{-1})=g^*t_q$. Thus this is an equality of the specified coefficient traces and canonical maps, not an existence-only identification of objects. Inverse-image composition, tensor and $\rho$ give an isomorphism $a:g_P^*G_qK\cong G_{q'}g^*K$. Substitute the specified counit formulas. Step 4 identifies the projection factors, and the displayed coefficient-trace equality identifies the last factors, giving $\epsilon_{q',g^*K}Rq'_!(a)=g^*\epsilon_{q,K}C_{q,g,G_qK}^{-1}$. Step 3 defines $\beta$ by exactly this equation. The adjunction bijection identifies $a$ with $\beta_{q,g,K}$ under the counit-preserving right-adjoint comparisons. Consequently this canonical mate is invertible.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2; existing ordinary finite-etale model lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction with its specified decomposition/trace; corroborating source SGA 4 XVIII 1.1.6, 2.13.2, 3.2.5

proof.text: Use the exact etale compact-support and exchange normalization of [lem-asd-etale-compact-support-normalization]. Let $j:\mathbf A^1_S\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^1_S$. Compose $j_!\dashv j^*$ with the projective-line adjunction. The open comparison is the comparison of left adjoints specified in [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map]; its mate is ordinary restriction comparison. Thus its counit commutes with the pullback square. The pasting identity along adjunctions [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] identifies the mate for $p_1=qj$ with the composite of this restriction comparison and the isomorphism in Step 5. The resulting right adjoint is $p_1^*(1)[2]$. For $d=0$ use the identity adjunction. For $d+1$ factor $p_{d+1}$ as an affine-line projection followed by $p_d$; Step 2 identifies the composite left adjoint, and the same mate-pasting identity identifies its exchange with the composite of the already invertible exchanges. The twist/pullback and tensor identifications of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] give $p_{d+1}^*(d+1)[2d+2]$. This induction uses the explicit composite adjunction, and compares its right adjoint directly with the ambient right adjoint of [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] by the unique counit-preserving comparison. The imported affine-space adjunction with its pro-etale twist dependency is not used.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2 and coherence (ii): open restriction and the affine-line tower

proof.text: Fix the etale normalization before applying locality. Apply [lem-asd-etale-compact-support-normalization] to every separated finite-type etale map $u$. It identifies the compactification-defined $Ru_!$ with the degreewise exact sum-extension functor, preserves its evaluation counit, and states the equation $(c_{u'}h^*)C_{u,g}=C^\Sigma_{u,g}(g^*c_u)$ for precisely the proper/open comparison used in Step 3. Thus in the exact etale realization $C_{u,g}$ is the inverse of the sheaf comparison of [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map], including the normalization of the map, not just its endpoints. Transport the adjunctions by their counit-preserving comparisons. For a separated finite-type etale map $u:U\to X$, the exact adjunction $u_!\dashv u^*$ in [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality] and the comparison [lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-modules] have mate the canonical inverse-image composition isomorphism. Indeed the comparison is defined by conjugating the ordinary inverse-image/direct-image exchange [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map]; its defining counit equation is exactly the equation of Step 3 after transposition. Pasting along the two adjunctions [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] proves that under $u^*f^\times\cong(fu)^\times$ and its primed analogue, $u'^*\beta_{f,g,K}$ is the mate for the pasted square $(fu,g)$, with the canonical pullback composition inserted. This proves locality of the actual map, rather than merely locality of its endpoints. For base restriction, write $a:S_0\hookrightarrow S$, $a_X:X_0\hookrightarrow X$, $a':S'_0\hookrightarrow S'$ and $a'_X:X'_0\hookrightarrow X'$. Here $fa_X=af_0$. Compose the exact etale adjunctions with the compact-support adjunctions: both left adjoints are identified by $Rf_!a_{X!}=Ra_!Rf_{0!}$ from the unbounded compact-support composition proved in Step 2. Their right adjoints consequently identify $a_X^*f^\times$ with $f_0^\times a^*$, and the primed equality gives the other restriction comparison. Pasting their counit equations identifies these comparisons with the mates for base changes $a$ and $a'$: the left-adjoint equality is the extension-by-zero comparison from Step 3 with the open base restriction inserted. Horizontal pasting from Step 3 reads $C_{f,ga'}=C_{f',a'}\,a'{}^*C_{f,g}$ and also $C_{f,ag_0}=C_{f_0,g_0}\,g_0^*C_{f,a}$. Since $ga'=ag_0$, apply part (1) of the mate-pasting lemma to their inverses. The first mate is the etale restriction comparison composed with $a'_X{}^*\beta_{f,g,K}$; the second is $\beta_{f_0,g_0,a^*K}$ composed with the unprimed restriction comparison. Their equality identifies the restricted canonical map with the chart map, as required.

source.place: Proof coherence (i) and (iii): etale localization of the canonical transpose

proof.text: Apply [sbc-thm-etale-local-normal-form] at each point of $X$. After an affine open restriction in the base, choose an affine open $U\subseteq X$ and an etale $e:U\to\mathbf A^d_{S_0}$ with $fu=p_de$. The relative dimension is $d$, since the etale factor has relative dimension zero and $f$ has pure relative dimension $d$. The chart inclusion $u$ is separated and of finite type: it is an open immersion, and it is quasi-compact because $X$ is Noetherian. The map $e$ is separated since $U$ and $\mathbf A^d_{S_0}$ are affine: on rings its diagonal is given by the surjection $B\otimes_R B\to B$, $b\otimes b'\mapsto bb'$. It is locally of finite presentation since it is etale, and quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1), since $U$ is affine and $\mathbf A^d_{S_0}$ is quasi-separated. Hence $e$ is of finite type. They are compactifiable, as are their composites, by [thm-nagata-compactification]. After arbitrary base change the corresponding charts still cover $X'$. Steps 6 and 7 identify the restriction of $\beta_{f,g,K}$ on each chart with etale inverse image of the affine-space isomorphism. Thus it is an isomorphism on every chart. Exact inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] commutes with cohomology; the kernel and cokernel of each cohomology map vanish on that etale covering, so their sections vanish by the sheaf axiom. Equivalently this is [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-detects-iso] applied to the underlying abelian cohomology sheaves. Hence every cohomology map is invertible globally, and [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] proves that $\beta_{f,g,K}$ is invertible in the unbounded derived category.

source.place: Proof coherence (iii): smooth charts and local detection, degree by degree

proof.text: At $K=A_S$, exact inverse image preserves the constant coefficient unit, so Step 8 gives $b:g'^*\omega_f\cong\omega_{f'}$. To check the tensor square, recall the meaning of the canonical tensor morphism: it is the transpose of $Rf_!(f^*K\otimes^L\omega_f)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{PF}^{-1}}K\otimes^LRf_!\omega_f\xrightarrow{1\otimes\epsilon_{f,A}}K$. Transpose both proposed paths under $Rf'_!\dashv f'^\times$. The transpose of the upper path is the pullback of this displayed composite preceded by $C^{-1}$. The transpose of the lower path is the primed projection inverse followed by $1\otimes Rf'_!b$ and $1\otimes\epsilon_{f',A}$. Step 4 identifies their projection-formula factors; the defining equation of $b$ from Step 3 identifies their final factors, since $\epsilon_{f',A}Rf'_!b=g^*\epsilon_{f,A}C^{-1}$. Naturality of $C$ and tensor lets these substitutions be made in the composite. The transposes are equal, so the adjunction bijection proves the displayed tensor compatibility. [thm-asd-smooth-tensor] ensures these canonical tensor maps are the claimed isomorphisms.

split_report.summary: Repair C4/E4/E6 by reusing the newly available lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction, which explicitly types finite small-etale twists, the unbounded model adjunction and its specified counit. Remove all mistyped imported model citations. The parent writes the coefficient-trace equation from decomposition compatibility and proves the canonical mate equation, affine-space induction, chart descent and tensor rectangle. A new etale compact-support normalization input records the compactified-to-sum exchange equation. Retain the unbounded refinement/composition repair. Second reading restores arbitrary finite A killed by an invertible N, matching the repaired smooth-tensor statement, rather than restricting to valuation residue rings. Repair of the refused landing: revalidated the current finite-coefficient unbounded proper projection statement; Step 4 now specifies its ordered map, checks all hypotheses and conjugates the exchange-coherence square by the signed tensor symmetries. Fresh second reading removes the invertible-ell composition citation in favor of its explicit ordinary-derived adjunction argument, and makes chart and restricted-proper hypotheses explicit.
split_report.blueprint: Original proof paragraph 1 is Steps 1–4 (unbounded compact-support comparison, composition, exchange and projection); paragraph 2 is Steps 5–8 (correctly typed finite-etale P1 trace model, open restriction, affine-space tower and smooth charts); final tensor sentence is Step 9. blueprint_update.statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be as in
[thm-asd-smooth-tensor], and let $g:S'\to S$
be any morphism of Noetherian schemes. Denote its base
change by $f':X'\to S'$, with $g':X'\to X$.
The canonical morphism

$$
g'^*f^\times K\longrightarrow f'^\times g^*K
$$

is an isomorphism for every complex $K$. At $K=A$
it identifies $g'^*\omega_f$ with $\omega_{f'}$,
and it respects the tensor isomorphism of
[thm-asd-smooth-tensor].

proof.text:
Proper base change on a compactification, followed by the
stalkwise base-change identity for extension by zero, gives
$Rf'_!g'^*\cong g^*Rf_!$, for bounded-below complexes by the
finite-amplitude argument in
[lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection]. Define the
displayed map by the adjunction of
[thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], transposing

$$
Rf'_!g'^*f^\times K\cong g^*Rf_!f^\times K
\longrightarrow g^*K.
$$

For a projective-line projection its unit and counit are
those explicitly constructed in
[thm-amb-p1-adjunction]. Both commute with base change:
the supported diagonal class does so by
[lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map], and the trace does so
by [thm-amb-p1-decomposition]. Hence the displayed
map in that case is the ordinary inverse-image and twist
base-change isomorphism. The same holds for an affine-line
projection by restricting its projective compactification,
and for affine space by composing those adjunctions.

It remains to verify the three coherences on which the identification
rests; each is a statement about the canonical maps, not merely about
their sources and targets.
*(i) The underlying base-change map in the model case.*
For the affine-space projection $\mathbf A^d_{S_0}\to S_0$
over a Zariski open $S_0\subseteq S$, the identification
$Rf'_!g'^*\cong g^*Rf_!$ of the first paragraph is the composite of
proper base change for the compactification
$\mathbf A^d\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^d$ with the stalkwise identity
$g^*j_!=j'_!g'^*$ for the extension by zero; both are comparisons of
the two diagrams obtained by base changing one diagram along $g$,
so the composite restricts to the chart $S'_0=S'\times_SS_0$.
*(ii) Unit and counit on the chart.* There the adjunction of
[thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] is the affine-space adjunction
[cor-amb-affine-space-adjunction], whose unit and counit are built
from the trace and the supported diagonal class; these commute with
base change by [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map] and
[thm-amb-p1-decomposition]. The displayed map is the transpose of
the counit composite, so the base-change isomorphism of (i) carries it
to the corresponding transpose over $S'_0$, which is the map defined
by the same recipe there.
*(iii) Descent to $X'$.* On the etale chart of $f$ used in
the proof of [thm-asd-smooth-tensor],
[lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality] identifies the map under
consideration with the base-change isomorphism of (ii) preceded by
etale inverse image, the sum over the finite fibre commuting with base
change; it is therefore an isomorphism on an etale cover of $X'$,
hence everywhere. Finally the tensor maps of
[thm-asd-smooth-tensor] were transposed from the projection
formula and the counit, and applying the same transposition to the
commuting base-change diagram of those two maps gives their base-change
compatibility. This proves all the claimed identifications.
